Building a structure requires material in two separate phases: first setting up the construction site (a fixed amount of sticks per microcell the building occupies), then the actual construction, which will require its own materials in the future.

Right now the game never creates a Task on its own to fetch this material: if it's missing, the site simply waits. You have to bring it there yourself, by manually commanding an individual (gather the material and deposit it at the site).

One exception: the very first Deposit Site you build, while the village has no other building with real storage space yet, gets its setup material for free, so you can always get started even with no stock.
This manual supply will be needed until you unlock the future Task management and warehouse management systems - from that point on, the game will be able to handle it on its own.

A wolf that no longer runs
For a long time a wolf pack kept coming back to scavenge in the waste pit. Each time it came a little closer, each time it fled a little later.
This time one of the young ones stayed. It no longer growls: it follows the villagers at a distance and sleeps near the huts. It is no longer a wolf: it is a dog.
If a wolf can live with us, perhaps other animals can too.
The villagers begin to look differently at the animals they hunt: some of them, one day, might stay in the village instead of ending up on the fire.
Among those who sit in the circle, one alone speaks for all: the village chief.

Wild animals and plants can, over time, live alongside people.

From the wolf that became a dog, the village has learned that what is wild, approached patiently over generations, can change and live at its side. It opens the way to domesticating animals and plants.
Allows starting to domesticate the animal species you have encountered.
The village learns that other animals, not just the wolf, can grow used to people. Each species must first be found in the world, then approached patiently: it will take generations.
Allows starting to domesticate the plant species you have encountered.

The village notices that plants grown near the huts, from discarded seeds, are not like those in the woods. By choosing and replanting the best seeds, over time plants will become more generous. It paves the way for agriculture.
